questions.prompt: What is the role of the 8051 accumulator A?
options: Main operand/result register for many arithmetic and logic instructions
The stack pointer
The high byte of DPTR
A code-memory address
questions.answer: Main operand/result register for many arithmetic and logic instructions
questions.explanation: A (ACC) is an 8-bit register used as an operand and result by many 8051 instructions.

questions.prompt: Which pair selects one of the four R0–R7 register banks?
options: RS1:RS0 in PSW
DPH:DPL
CY:AC
SP:PC
questions.explanation: The PSW bank-select bits RS1 and RS0 select one of four banks.

questions.prompt: How does signed overflow (OV) differ from carry (CY)?
options: OV reports signed two's-complement overflow; CY reports unsigned carry/borrow behavior.
They always have the same value.
CY reports signed overflow and OV reports parity.
OV is the stack pointer.
questions.answer: OV reports signed two's-complement overflow; CY reports unsigned carry/borrow behavior.
questions.explanation: Signed overflow and unsigned carry describe different interpretations of the same bit operation.

options: Writes A to internal data RAM at the address held in R0.
Loads the immediate value R0 into A.
Writes A to code memory.
Copies the stack pointer to R0.
questions.answer: Writes A to internal data RAM at the address held in R0.
questions.explanation: The @ prefix means indirect addressing through R0 or R1 in this classic 8051 form.

questions.prompt: Why can direct address 80h and indirect address 80h refer to different storage on some 8052-class devices?
options: Direct addressing selects an SFR while indirect addressing may select upper internal RAM.
The address changes from hexadecimal to decimal.
Direct addressing always means code memory.
The CPU ignores the addressing mode.
questions.answer: Direct addressing selects an SFR while indirect addressing may select upper internal RAM.
questions.explanation: The address space and target depend on the addressing mode and the specific derivative.
